# Bank and theft

## In short
- **Bank limit:** you can take at most **5 items from the bank in any rolling 15 minutes**. The limit rises to 10 when the town is in chaos, and People's Court adds 5 more. Banished citizens can't take anything from the bank. [1] [2] [3]
- **Bank theft:** at night (outside 07:00–18:59 by default) you can "steal" from the bank. You always get the item, but there is a **60% chance your name shows up in the register**. Bank theft is impossible in small towns, which have night mode turned off. [3] [4] [5]
- **Home theft:** you can normally only steal from a living citizen while they are **outside town**, and only if their home has no lock. A plain theft is **discovered 50% of the time**. An alarm always gives you away. An Exploding Doormat or a rabid dog wounds you, or kills you if you are already wounded. [6] [7] [3]
- **To protect your chest:** keep a Padlock and Chain (`lock` property) in it, or build the lock home upgrade. [8] [6]

## How it works

### Taking from the bank
1. **Where you must be.** The town bank counts as a "Bank" source only when you are in town (no zone). When you are outside, the same inventory is treated as "Tamer", not as the bank. [9]
2. **Banished citizens.** Any take from the bank fails with "bank blocked" if you are banished. This includes bank theft. [3]
3. **The anti-abuse check (`BankAntiAbuseService::allowedToTake`):** [1]
   - Max items = `bank_abuse.limit` (default **5**). If the town is in chaos, `bank_abuse.chaos_limit` (default **10**) is used instead. [2]
   - **+5** to that max if People's Court (`small_court_#00`) is built. [10]
   - The time window is `bank_abuse.lock_range_min` (default **15 minutes**) counted back from now. [2]
   - If the window contains any "BankLock" entry for you, taking is refused outright.
   - Otherwise taking is allowed only while your "BankTaken" entries in the window are fewer than the max.
4. **Recording each take.** Every take that passes validation is recorded right away (`onTriggerBankLockUpdate`, priority 90). It is stored as "BankTaken" if you were still allowed to take at that moment, otherwise as "BankLock". [3] [1]
5. **Register and warning.** A normal take is written to the bank register under your name. You also see a warning not to be greedy, or other citizens may see you as an egoist. Deposits are logged too. [3]
6. **Usual inventory rules still apply.** Your rucksack must not be full. You can't carry more than one bag extension of the same type. The heavy-item limit applies. You can carry only one soul unless you are the shaman (role or job). [3]

### Stealing from the bank at night
- **How you trigger it.** It is the inventory move done in `theft` mode (`TransferItemModality::BankTheft`). [11] [12]
- **Night only.** It is refused unless night mode is active. Two conditions are needed: [4]
  - the `features.nightmode` setting is on (default `true`) [13];
  - the server hour is before the daytime start or after its end. The default daytime range is `[7,18]`, so night means 19:00–06:59. `modifiers.daytime.invert` swaps day and night. [14]
- **Direction.** It must go from the bank into your rucksack. [3]
- **Same checks as a normal take.** You must not be banished. The anti-abuse limit applies and the theft counts toward it. [3]
- **Outcome.** You always get the item. An old "theft fails" chance is commented out in the code. Then: [3]
  - **60%:** the theft is discovered and logged with your name ("Your theft attempt failed! You were discovered!").
  - **40%:** it is logged anonymously ("Your name will not appear in the register").

### Stealing from (or dropping into) another citizen's home
**Starting an intrusion** (`intrude_visit_api`) is refused if any of these is true: [15]
- the victim is alive and the home has an explicit lock;
- the victim is alive and in town, and you don't have `CitizenProperties::EnableAdvancedTheft`;
- you are already intruding on this victim;
- you have `tg_steal` and the town is not in chaos;
- you are stealing (not dropping) and you have sent this victim an item by PM.

Starting a new intrusion removes your other intrusions.

**Alarm on intrusion.** If the victim is alive and has the `alarm` home upgrade, starting an intrusion triggers the alarm at most **once per 15 minutes per intruder**. It writes a public log entry and sends the victim a crow PM. [15]

**When the house counts as protected** (`houseIsProtected`): [6]
- A dead citizen's home is never protected.
- A living citizen who is in town is protected, unless the thief has `EnableAdvancedTheft`.
- These always protect, whoever the thief is:
  - the house level's built-in theft protection;
  - a home tag `lock`;
  - the home upgrade `lock`;
  - an item with the `lock` property in the chest, e.g. Padlock and Chain [8].
- During an active Halloween event, a `haunting_soul` in the chest protects against a thief it has already scared.

**Checks when you move an item** (`onValidateItemTransfer`): [3]
- You can't steal from someone you sent an item to by PM.
- Items with the `nosteal` property can't be stolen. The Impersonal Exploding Doormat has it. [16]
- You can't drop items into a dead citizen's home.
- You can't drop items into someone else's home while the town is in chaos.
- You can't drop a bag extension into someone else's home.
- **Halloween:** if a `haunting_soul` is in the victim's chest during an active Halloween event, the theft fails. You get `terror` and `tg_steal`, and your intrusion ends. The victim gets the picto `r_decofeist_#00`, but only the first time you are scared there.

**What happens after a theft** (`onPostHandleCitizenTheft`). Every theft or drop gives you the status `tg_steal`. Stealing also gives you a picto: `r_theft_#00` from a living victim, `r_plundr_#00` from a dead one. For a theft from a living victim, the first matching case below applies: [3]

| Case | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1. Impersonal Exploding Doormat (`trapma_#00`) in the chest, or home tag `rabid_dog` | You are wounded, or killed if already wounded (cause ExplosiveDoormat / RabidDog). The doormat is used up. The theft is logged with your name. |
| 2. You carry `christmas_suit_full_#00` or `leprechaun_suit_#00` | The public log is anonymous. An admin-only log names you. |
| 3. Victim has the `alarm` home upgrade | Always logged with your name. |
| 4. Otherwise | Discovered with a chance of **0.5** (base `discovery_change` [7]). Discovered: logged with your name. Not discovered: "without being discovered". |

- **Dead victim:** looting is always logged.
- **Crow PM:** the victim (the home's owner) gets a crow theft PM after every theft. The code does not check whether they are alive.
- **Dropping an item into a living citizen's home:** discovered with a **10%** chance, or always if they have an alarm. A costume prevents discovery. If discovered, it is logged with your name.
- **Afterwards:** your intrusion record is removed. [3]

**Once per day.** `tg_steal` is a volatile status, so it is cleared during the nightly reset. While you have it, you can't start a new intrusion unless the town is in chaos. In practice this means one theft per day outside chaos. [17] [18] [15]

## What changes it

| Factor | Effect |
|---|---|
| People's Court (`small_court_#00`) | +5 to the bank take limit [1] |
| Town in chaos | Bank limit uses `chaos_limit` (10) [1]. `tg_steal` no longer blocks intrusions [15]. Dropping items into other homes is forbidden [3] |
| Banishment | No taking or stealing from the bank [3] |
| `EnableAdvancedTheft` citizen property | Lets you steal from a living citizen who is in town. Explicit locks still block it [6] [15] |
| Padlock and Chain (`lock` property), `lock` home upgrade or tag, house level theft protection | House can't be robbed [6] |
| `alarm` home upgrade | Intrusion is announced (at most once per 15 min per intruder). Theft is always revealed. Drops are always revealed [15] [3] |
| Impersonal Exploding Doormat (`trapma_#00`) in the chest / home tag `rabid_dog` | Thief is wounded, or killed if already wounded. The doormat is used up [3] |
| Thief status `tamer_watch_1` / `tamer_watch_2` ("Stand guard", the dog) | Discovery chance ×0.5 / ×0.75 (50% becomes 25% / 37.5%). Both statuses are removed after one theft or drop [3] [19] |
| Christmas suit / Leprechaun suit in your rucksack | Theft logged anonymously and drops never revealed. Event pictos `r_santac_#00` / `r_lepre_#00` during the matching active event [3] |
| `haunting_soul` (active Halloween) | Theft fails. Thief gets `terror` and `tg_steal`, and that thief is locked out afterwards [3] [6] |
| Sending an item by PM | You can never steal from that recipient [3] |
| `nosteal` items | Can't be stolen [3] |

## Town types
- **Default, remote, panda:** they share the default bank settings: limit 5, chaos limit 10, window 15 min. Neither the remote nor the panda differences change `bank_abuse` or night mode. [2] [20] [21]
- **Small:** `features.nightmode: false`, so bank theft is never available. The bank limits are the default ones. [5] [4]
- **Custom:** the `bank_abuse.*` settings and the daytime settings can be changed. The config explainer has a `bank_abuse.*` label group. [22]

## Related
- **Defense items in the bank:** each one adds to town defense. The Bank page shows an item-defense factor of 1 + (1+level)×0.5 when `item_meca_parts_#00` is built. [23]
- **Visiting homes:** attacking citizens, complaints and banishment are on the same page as theft. [24]
- **When a citizen dies:** their items go to the bank if they die on the town zone, or to their chest if they die in town. A banished citizen gets a `banned_note_#00`. [25]
- **Chaos:** it starts when 1–10 citizens are alive, some are in town and the day is above 3. Banishments are then lifted. [18]

## Not verified
- **Going over the bank limit may extend your lockout.** The take is recorded before the limit check runs. Because the code stores the over-limit attempt as a "BankLock" entry, a refused take probably restarts a full 15-minute lockout. I could not confirm that the other listeners (the recording step) still run after the validation error.
- **`bank_abuse.base_range_min` (5):** I found it in the rules but not in any code I read, so its effect is unknown.
- **Who has `EnableAdvancedTheft`:** I found no job, hero skill or item card that grants it.
- **Rabid dog and alarm sources:** I did not find what sets the `rabid_dog` home tag or the costs of the `lock` and `alarm` home upgrades.
